all.text: At this latitude, the Earth's spin carries the ship east at about 910 mph, whatever the captain is doing.
The sun reaches its highest point here about 59 minutes after it does in Southampton.
Drill straight through the Earth from here and you'd surface at 28.6°S, 163.9°E, about 1,340 km from Sydney.
This far north, they're roughly level with New Orleans, even though it's a world away.
The seabed is roughly 1,274 m below the ship, which is about 3.9 Eiffel Towers stacked up.
